opportunities.title: HIRING OF INDIVIDUAL CONSULTANTS TO DEVELOP A NATIONAL INTEROPERABILITY FRAMEWORK FOR HEALTH INFORMATION EXCHANGE IN TWO MEMBER STATES (Tunisia and Seychelles)
opportunities.description: The African Union has received financing from the World Bank toward the cost of the Africa Centres for Disease Control Support Program to Combat Current and Future Public Health Threats Project. The Project Development Objective is to enhance the capacity of Africa Centres for Disease Control and Prevention (Africa CDC) to support AU Member States in preventing, detecting, and responding to current and future public health threats and intends to apply part of the proceeds for consulting services. Health Information Systems interoperability is a foundational requirement for implementing national Health Information Exchange (HIE). A robust, standards-based interoperability framework is essential to enable secure data exchange, support system integration, and establish the technical and governance foundation for sustainable HIE implementation. Findings from the HIE maturity assessments conducted across AU Member States have identified interoperability as a high-impact priority, critical to enabling subsequent phases such as governance strengthening and phased digital health system implementation. As part of the support by Africa CDC in implementing HIE across Member States, digital maturity assessments were conducted in 12 AU Member States, alongside the development of HIE roadmaps. opportunities.title: Consultancy Services to Support Africa CDC and the African Union in Assessing the Feasibility of the Implementation of a Continental Health Financing Observatory for AU Member States
opportunities.description: The Africa Centres for Disease Control and Prevention (Africa CDC) invites eligible and qualified bilingual English/French consultancy firms to submit proposals for the Feasibility Assessment of the Establishment and Implementation of a Continental Health Financing Observatory for African Union Member States. The consultancy will undertake a comprehensive feasibility assessment for the proposed Sustainable African Centre for Investment in Health Accountability (SACIA) Observatory, including the development of an institutional model, governance framework, financial sustainability pathway, and phased implementation roadmap to strengthen health financing intelligence, foster fiscal dialogue and evidence-informed decision-making and policy reforms across AU Member States. Duration : Three (3) months with the possibility of extension based on project needs. Location : Remote, with in-country missions in two (2) AU Member States. Interested firms are requested to submit their proposals in accordance with the requirements and instructions set out in the Solicitation Document. Interested firms must be legally registered, bilingual (English/French) consultancy firm or consortium with demonstrated expertise in health financing, public financial management (PFM), governance, institutional analysis, and multidisciplinary project management.
